title: Heterogeneity Pacing Controller and KV Residency Strategy for Mixed-Length Continuous Batching
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Tune the continuous batching scheduler to handle mixed prompt/response length workloads with minimal p95 latency regressions and reduced GPU memory churn. Introduce a new controller (Heterogeneity Pacing Controller, HPC) plus a KV residency policy to reduce fragmentation and eviction storms that occur when long responses interleave with short prompt-only requests.
background: Production traffic shows a bimodal distribution: many short-query calls (few tokens) and fewer long-completion calls (hundreds to thousands of tokens). The existing continuous coalescer aggressively packs by arrival which increases throughput but causes high KV churn, repeated GPU slab allocations, and p95 latency tail spikes during bursts of long responses. Recent postmortems point to eviction cascades and frequent kernel rebinds when model KV footprints cross slab thresholds.
proposed_solution: 1) Add an HPC layer that tracks per-cohort horizon (expected completion length) and enforces adaptive pacing windows: short-window cohort (S) prioritized for low latency, long-window cohort (L) allowed larger micro-coalescing windows to amortize KV residency. 2) Implement a soft-pin KV residency policy: reserve a small fraction of KV banks for high-residency (recently active long responses) with a decaying reservation that avoids full eviction storms. 3) GPU memory buckets: split GPU slab allocation logic into prefix-resident and response-resident pools to reduce cross-traffic compaction. 4) Scheduler preemption thresholds: allow preemption of long-slot packs when S cohort latency approaches SLO. 5) Experiment flags and observability: expose HPC tuning knobs (window_ms, pin_fraction, decay_tau) behind a feature gate and add end-to-end tracing for KV allocations + evictions.
success_metrics: p50 generation latency for S cohort <= baseline + 5ms
p95 generation latency for S cohort reduced by >= 15% compared to baseline under mixed load
mean GPU memory compaction events per minute reduced by >= 30%
tokens/sec throughput within 90-100% of baseline for steady long-only load
eviction-induced retransmits (retries due to lost KV state) reduced by >= 50%
acceptance_criteria: HPC toggled on in staging with default params shows no S-cohort p95 regression vs staging baseline
KV soft-pin prevents eviction cascade in targeted stress tests (see test_plan)
Feature flag allows gradual rollout to 10% production shadow traffic with auto-rollback on >10% error uplift
Kubernetes resource usage for GPU nodes unchanged beyond expected variability
Documentation updated: runtime config reference, release notes, and operator runbook for pin tuning
test_plan: 1) Synthetic load: generate controlled bimodal workloads (80% short 5-20 token prompts, 20% long 300-1500 token completions) at QPS levels of 50%, 75%, 100% of production. 2) Stress scenarios: long-burst spike (10x long QPS for 30s), interleaved microbursts, and cold-KV-warmup sequences. 3) Shadow rollout: run HPC on 5% of production traffic in shadow mode with trace correlation. 4) Metrics: collect per-cohort latencies, GPU slab compaction logs, KV eviction counts, kernel rebind frequency, and memory headroom. 5) Compare A/B: baseline scheduler vs HPC-enabled scheduler across identical traces.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and run on staging cluster. 2) Run full test_plan and iterate params. 3) Deploy to Canary pool (5% live traffic) with tracing enabled. 4) If metrics stable, increment to 25% for 1 hour, then 50% for 2 hours, then 100% of non-critical clusters. 5) Lock default params after 72h of stable metrics and communicate to SRE/On-call. 6) Provide one-click rollback via feature flag and an automated circuit that disables HPC if GPU memory headroom drops below threshold for >5 min.
implementation_notes: - HPC maintains lightweight per-cohort EWMA for horizon estimation to avoid per-request ML models. - Soft-pin uses a token-hysteresis budget per GPU that decays every 100ms; eviction candidates are scored by recency*expected-residency. - Scheduler changes limited to the runtime coalescer with minimal surface area changes to API layer. - Add new runtime counters: kv_pin_hits, kv_pin_evictions, cohort_window_ms, preempt_count. - Ensure compatibility with Dedicated and Private modes by gating pin behavior when customers enable strict data isolation.
risks: Mis-tuned pin_fraction can cause underutilization of GPU memory and reduce throughput
Incorrect horizon estimation can accidentally misclassify requests leading to increased latency for long completions
Edge-case interactions with existing prefix caching heuristics could introduce regressions for prefix-heavy workloads
Operator complexity: tuning knobs increase SRE burden unless sensible defaults are well tested
